messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I saw a ~2.8x p95 regression on streaming vs non-streaming on the nightly replay harness after the kernel-selection tweak. Not sure if it's batching, chunk alignment, or KV interplay.

devon: Ack. Which workload? small-chat vs long-context?

maria: small-chat (avg 120 tokens) with synthetic client that does 4-chunk streaming (256B chunks). Non-stream path is same traffic but returned as one response.

kevin: Any KV hit-rate differences? Streaming keeps KV warm differently.

maria: KV hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 74% in the failing run. That aligns with higher model compute + more re-fetches.

sam: Can you paste the harness config?

maria: Sure:

```
{"workload":"small-chat","clients":120,"streaming":true,"chunk_size":256,"batch_window_ms":6,"kernel_policy":"auto"}
```

nina: Two quick guesses: 1) Kernel selection flip to the more accurate but heavier kernel for short sequences, 2) batching heuristic mis-grouping streaming chunks into many tiny batches.

devon: I ran a quick profile on my laptop with perf counters attached. When streaming is enabled we see kernel A (FP16-optimized matmul) chosen for seq_len=8, but at chunk boundaries we get fallback to kernel C for seq_len=64 due to padding heuristics. That causes extra memcpy and kernel launch overhead.

maria: Interesting. Do we have trace with thread timestamps?

perf-bot: nightly-bench: 1845123200 - streaming_small_chat - p50 28ms p95 312ms throughput 1.2k tok/s (baseline non-streaming p95 110ms)

kevin: Oof. Can you run apples-to-apples? reproduce the replay harness but force kernel policy=legacy and batching=group-by-client for streaming so we match non-streaming batching behavior.

maria: Running that now. Also toggling `kv_prefetch=true` to see if hit-rate improves.

sam: FYI, client readloop pacing also affects observed batch sizes. If the test client flushes every chunk immediately we get tiny batches. Try `client_pacer=coalesce(20ms)` to let readloop accumulate chunks before sending.

maria: Good call. Patch notes: added `client_pacer` flag and `kv_prefetch` to harness. Re-running.

perf-bot: adhoc-bench: 1845123520 - streaming_small_chat (client_pacer=coalesce(20ms), kv_prefetch=true, kernel_policy=legacy) - p50 34ms p95 118ms throughput 1.9k tok/s

nina: That looks a lot closer to non-stream baseline. So main issues were batching + KV churn.

kevin: Agreed. Action items: (1) tighten kernel selection heuristics to avoid fallback at chunk boundary (investigate padding logic), (2) add a readloop pacing recommendation default for streaming clients to avoid tiny-batch mode, (3) make KV prefetch more aggressive for streaming sessions.

maria: I'll open a tracking issue with reproducer and attach `perf.data` + harness config. Anyone wants to pick up kernel selection fix?

devon: I'll take kernel selection. Will try to add unit tests simulating chunk boundary padding.

sam: I'll formalize the client_pacer setting and add it to devex docs. Also will add a small synthetic test that exercises worst-case tiny-batch streaming.

perf-bot: issue-created: RW-4128 - "chunk-alignment: reduce kernel fallback and tiny-batch streaming regressions" (link internal)

maria: Thanks all. If we can get a quick patch to kernel padding threshold we should re-run nightly and confirm no regression. :thumbsup:

kevin: Also recommend we log `chosen_kernel` in runtime traces for streaming requests for 24h to gather more data before/after change.

maria: Logged. Closing the investigation thread for now, will update RW-4128 with results.
